p: In the passive, the focus is on the action or the object, not on who does it.
Use 'by' if you want to say who does the action.

grammar.title: Quantifiers
grammar.short: (not) enough, (a) few, (a) little, a lot of, plenty of, too much / many

slides.sub: Future living: is there enough space in your city?
slides.hook: Does your town have enough green spaces? Are there too many cars? What about affordable homes?

slides.h: a few / a little vs few / little
p: 'a few' and 'a little' are positive: some, a small amount.
'few' and 'little' (without 'a') are negative: almost none, not enough.
ex: There are **a few** smart buildings in my town. (some – good)
There are **few** affordable flats in the centre. (almost none – bad)
We need **a little** more energy to charge the car.

p: too much / too many + noun = more than we want.
enough + noun = the right amount. not enough = less than we need.
With adjectives: too + adjective, adjective + enough.
ex: There's **too much** concrete and **too many** cars.
We don't have **enough** green, energy-saving homes.
The flat isn't **big enough**. And it's **too expensive** – not affordable at all.

slides.title: How to improve our streets
text: In our neighbourhood there are **too many** cars and **too much** noise. There are **very few** trees and **not enough** places for teenagers to hang out.
We propose an innovative plan: **plenty of** cycle lanes, **a few** solar-powered bus stops and **a lot of** green roofs.
It isn't **too expensive**. With **a little** help from the council, it could be ready in two years.

items: There are too much skyscrapers here.
There are too many skyscrapers here.

slides.e: space is uncountable; 'not enough' = less than we need.

p: many / few + countable; much / little + uncountable.
a lot of, plenty of, enough + both.
a few / a little = some; few / little = not enough.
noun: enough steel; adjective: strong enough.
